full_judgment: But in case of under-valuation of the relief claimed in the suit or non-payment of proper court fees, it appears from the statute itself that before taking any action under clause "b" or "c" of rule 11 of Order 7 of the C.P.C. some time not exceeding 21 days as per amendment must be given to the party concerned for correction of the valuation of the suit or the relief claimed and for payment of deficit court fees. Here in this case from the impugned order, it does not appear that the plaintiff-petitioners of the present suit were given any time by the court for correction of the valuation of the relief sought for in the suit and/or for payment of the deficit Court fees thereon. So, before compliance of that legal requirement, it can not be held that the suit is barred by or under rule 11 of Order 7 of the C.P.C. and as such not maintainable. In support of this view, a decision reported in 22 DLR (SC) 144 may be referred to. In this case the trial Court dismissed the suit under Order 7, rule 11 C.P.C. for its under-valuation and in and sufficient court fees. On appeal, the High Court found the order of the trial judge contrary to the provisions of section 149 and Order VII, rule 11 C.P.C. under which he was required to allow the plaintiff an opportunity to correct the value of the suit and pay deficit court fees which shall have the same force and effect as if such fee had been paid in the first in-stance. Their Lordships set aside the order of dismissal of the suit and remanded the suit for allowing the plaintiff to make good the deficiency in the court fee. The Supreme Court of Pakistan then in appeal dismissed the leave petition and upheld the judgment of the High Court.
